title: Dispatch: Require campaign position, restore discovery boundary guard, ungate checkpoint proof (attempt 3)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 3) — three remaining defects after supervisor review of attempt 2.

Attempt 2 (75ef96d) fixed four of six findings and is KEPT. Verified by supervisor probe: the ruling/house-rule temporal divergence is genuinely gone (at replay position 5 the seam now returns the ruling active at 5, r-old, not its later successor r-new). CampaignRuleError, prospectivity validation on revoke/supersede, the position-aware ruling query, the typed CampaignRuleReadSeam return, the isAmbiguityRuling guard, and the self-sorting comment are all correct. Do not revert any of that. Three defects remain.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.3, cut from 75ef96d on eshyra-jhpt.2.2. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 1 (SEVERE, not fixed by attempt 2) — the position-less fallback is self-referential, so it can never exclude a future rule, and a new test now enshrines that.
activeRows resolves an omitted cutoff to `MAX(effective_position) FROM campaign_rule`. The latest rule therefore always defines the cutoff to its own position and always includes itself. Supervisor probe, one house rule effective at ordinal 999, still failing on attempt 2:
    at position 1 : []
    no position   : [ 'future' ]      <- future rule still leaks
The dispatch for attempt 2 required, for whichever option was chosen, a test proving the position-less result "never returns a rule whose effective position is in the future". That condition is unsatisfiable under a rules-table MAX, and instead campaignRuleStore.test.ts:121 "uses the latest recorded position when no cutoff is supplied" asserts `toEqual(['now', 'future'])` — it encodes the defect as the expected behaviour. AGENTS.md is explicit that expectations must not be adjusted to match current output; the implementation is what changes.
FIX: take the other option — make the campaign position REQUIRED on the active-at-position path. Change listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition and listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition to require campaignPosition, and require it on createCampaignRuleReadSeam. A caller that does not know the position must not receive a silently wrong answer; eshyra-jhpt.3 and .4 always know the position, and .8 must pass the disputed turn's position. Delete the "latest recorded position" fallback and the test that asserts the leak; replace that test with one proving a future-effective rule is absent at an earlier position and present at or after its effective position. (If some caller genuinely cannot supply a position, derive "current" from campaign history — turn_trace / scene_log — never from the rules table, and say so in your notes; but required-position is the expected outcome.)

FINDING 2 (guard test weakened — and the supervisor's dispatch caused it) — restore the discovery boundary guard by moving the seam type instead.
Attempt 2 added `!line.trimStart().startsWith('import type')` to the "is not imported by runtime modules" assertion in packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryBoundary.test.ts, because campaignRuleStore.ts now imports CampaignRuleReadSeam from ../discovery/types.js. That import happened because the attempt-2 dispatch told you to import it from there. That instruction was wrong and the guard should not have been relaxed to accommodate it: the guard exists because the offline discovery pilot is experiment-only and runtime modules must not depend on it, and a compile-time dependency on an experimental module is still a dependency.
FIX: move the CampaignRuleReadSeam interface (and NULL_CAMPAIGN_RULE_SEAM, if that keeps them together sensibly) into packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts alongside CampaignRuleProjection and CampaignRulingProjection, and have packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts re-export it — exactly the pattern eshyra-jhpt.1 already established for the projection types. Then campaignRuleStore.ts imports the seam type from its own domain, no runtime module imports discovery, and discoveryBoundary.test.ts REVERTS to its original assertion with no `import type` exemption. Keep the existing discovery re-export so discovery's own consumers are unaffected. Confirm src/internal.ts still exports the seam type exactly once.
This is the one place you may edit campaignRules.ts, and only to receive the moved type.

FINDING 3 (required coverage does not run) — the checkpoint round-trip proof is entirely Dolt-gated.
The new test lives in packages/core/test/checkpoint.restore.test.ts under `describe.skipIf(!doltOk)`. The `dolt` binary is absent on this machine, so the acceptance criterion "checkpoint/restore round trips preserve identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions" has zero local coverage; skipped tests went from 19 to 20. The Dolt gate is legitimate for `restoreToNewWorkingCopy`, but the capture half needs no Dolt at all: serializeCampaign() and canonicalize() in persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts are pure SQLite reads over sqlite_master.
FIX: split the proof. Add an ungated test (in the campaign-rule test file, or a checkpoint serialize test) that creates rules in every relevant state - active, superseded, revoked, ambiguity-provenance ruling, disputed-turn position - then asserts serializeCampaign captures the campaign_rule table with those identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions intact, and that canonicalize is stable across two serializations. Keep the Dolt-gated full restore test as the end-to-end half. Do not add checkpoint machinery; serialize.ts already enumerates tables from sqlite_master.

SCOPE
Storage and query APIs, plus the type move in finding 2. No prompt/context assembly (.3/.4), no ambiguity dialogue (.6), no replay orchestration (.8), no CLI (.5). Do not fix the discovery-side cast tracked by eshyra-neus. Update any call sites affected by making the position required.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Skipped test counts must not rise above the documented baseline for reasons introduced by this bead.
